notes.title: Towers, Turrets, Turtles, Tutorials
notes.content:
Hi everyone, time for another update
The big one here is we reworked the tutorial, It's now split into two parts:
[olist]
[*]what you probably know if you've played a tower defence before
[*]what Towers, Turrets, Turtles does differently.
[/olist]

it does this with a really neat objective system, alongside our older dialogue and image popup systems.

the achievement for beating the tutorial is now achieved by beating the second tutorial, as is the highscores.


[h2]Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Turbo mode no longer gives more gold and increases turret costs, but instead reduces gold income.
[*] Turrets still shoot faster, and you still start with more lives.
[*] triple turbo is now the default mode
[*] rebalanced entire game, fire rate upgrades should be stronger overall, and upgrading turrets is always worth the money.
[*]turtle turrets are now (ironically) the best turrets to rush out.
[*]added noises to the Gnome peas
[*]what do you mean you've never seen the gnome peas?
[/list]
[h2]Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] fixed bug where turbo mode would spawn infinite copies of the final waves.
[*] fixed bug where final wave on single turbo would not display correctly
[/list]

notes.content:

Have fun!

notes.title: Towers, Turrets, Turtles, Twitch
notes.content:
Hi everyone, 
It's time for another update, this one took a bit longer than expected, but I'm happy to show the features.

[h2]Twitch Integration[/h2]
as the title implies, the biggest feature of todays update is twtich integration,

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43300656/8a1d111c5d591d8001f8987b0f5bc92f32cde6f0.png[/img]

you can connect your twitch account to Towers, Turrets, Turtles to read your (or someone elses!) Twitch chat, and the Peas will read it for you, alongside who said it.
have fun shooting your Twitch viewers over and over!

[h2]Improved Building[/h2]
We've also added two new building improvements, a centre marker, and resting grids.
even when you're not building you can now see where you could build, and where your mouse is currently hovered over.
we're hoping that this should make your time building a lot easier, as trying to find it all without any convenient reference when there's already so much going on can be tricky.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43300656/30fbd5d20d71cea37beed48523ecd85195e98dc9.png[/img]

all of this can be disabled in the options menu, so use it how you like!


[h2]Minor Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] changed time system for several things so they now work while the game is paused, most notable is the water effects and changing music tracks
[*] adjust slam turret animation speed, so it works even when it's firing VERY quickly
[*]fixed bug where resource gain popups would block the interface
[*]fixed blocked areas in Mitchs challenge
[*]Computer Tower is now transparent while building
[*]buffed fast turret
[*] adjusted position of computer tower in hard mode
[*] fixed bug where computer tower lights wouldn't update correctly in turbo mode
[/list]

that's all for now, our next update will focus on new user experience and making the game easier overall, and should be MUCH faster than this one.
Until next time!

notes.title: Towers, Turrets, Turtle, Tooltips!
notes.content:
Hi everyone,
We just released a update to Towers Turrets, Turtles, this one is relatively small in nature but includes bug fixes and Quality of life improvements I'm sure everyone would like.

[h1][b]Tooltips[/b][/h1]
we now support tooltips, they're super easy to implement, so we should be putting them anywhere they'd be helpful, although this doesn't seem like a big deal, it allows us to rethink how we display data to the players.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43300656/2b62c8a8d1ad07af1f6fec022134220573394c7b.png[/img]


[h1][b]Pausing[/b][/h1]
We've also improved the pausing system, which means that the game will stop entirely when doing things like reading dialogue or browsing menus.
We've also added a pause button which will stop the game and buy you time to plan!
You'll find it in the top right corner, by the main menu button.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43300656/a4cd9e5c57ece7044c8ab0af5091015454784c01.png[/img]

[h2]fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] improved positioning on building confirmation and upgrade panels, especially on unusual resolutions
[*] added text to explain what the turbo mode dropdown actually is
[*] fixed positioning of the circus cannon on tutorial and easy levels
[*] adjusted damage values on the turtle turret
[/list]

[list]
[*] fixed bug where selling a turret wouldn't update the pathfinding until you either sold another turret or placed one.
[*] adjusted terrain collision on the easy/tutorial level, this will also change the bounds the camera can move to.
[*] fixed bug where you could select no turret by pressing hotkey for turrets that don't exist (yet)
[/list]

notes.title: New(New) release date and Update #1 details
notes.content:
Hi Everyone, its been a short while.
We've made the decision to push back the launch date, to avoid competing with the Steam Winter Sale.

Our new Launch date is [b]6th January 2023[/b]

This has given us time to work on the first content update and get some internal feedback from Beta Testers, It's been really fun to watch people who haven't played the game for hundreds of hours get their hands on it, and their most important feedbacks should be implemented way before launch.

While I can't really talk about it until I have something to show, I'm really looking forward to sharing it with everyone, as it should double the amount of playable content and really mix up what a Tower Defence can be!

That's all for now, see you all at the launch!

notes.title: Optimisation and speed
notes.content:
Hey everyone, It's been two days since we revealed Towers, Turrets, Turtles on steam, and we've been working hard polishing whatever we could find, so we thought this would be a great time to talk about framerate since it's a very important part of game development and making things as good as possible.

When optimising there's a few things we keep in mind,
1. Our developers (both of them!) have very beefy PCs, older machines will run slower than what we're used to.
2. Laptops (which are a huge part of the gaming market) may not have big graphics cards required for fancy effects.
3. There's a few things that can eat FPS if mishandled, you're probably familiar with ones like lighting and large open spaces, but this can also include less obvious things like interface and targeting.
4. There may be a lot (and we mean A LOT) going on both on and off screen at any time, so stress testing how much we can fit on the screen at once is vital.

Here's one of those stress tests, somewhere around 800 Turtles on the screen at once, all  while sticking above 60fps

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43300656/c5f2315b2cd8e148b4ccf4dbbf43a976b19b369a.png[/img]

Of course, there's always going to be room for improvement, but with statistics like this, we're sure even the older machines you might be playing on will have a good time running our game.

that's all for now, next time I'll talk about AI, and how games like ours quickly calculate the paths of so many enemies.
Until then!
